# ARTICLE VIII — FINANCIAL COVENANTS

## 8.1 Loan-to-Cost Ratio

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
The Loan-to-Cost Ratio shall not exceed eighty percent (80%) at any time. **"Loan-to-Cost Ratio"** or **"LTC"** means the ratio of (a) the outstanding principal balance of the Loan plus the Interest Reserve Balance to (b) Total Project Costs. **"Total Project Costs"** means the aggregate of all costs and expenses incurred or to be incurred in connection with the acquisition, development, construction and completion of the Project, as set forth in the Approved Project Budget as in effect from time to time, including the cost of the Property, Hard Costs, Soft Costs, the Interest Reserve, the Origination Fee, the Developer Fee and contingency, and excluding, solely for purposes of this ratio, the Mezzanine Loan.

Testing: As of the Closing Date, the Loan-to-Cost Ratio is $47,500,000 ÷ $56,700,000 = 83.77%, which exceeds the eighty percent (80%) maximum. At an eighty percent (80%) Loan-to-Cost Ratio, the maximum Loan Amount would be $45,360,000, a reduction of $2,140,000. **Drafting Note:** The Condition Precedent in Section 3.1(g) requires a $2,140,000 Equity Escrow Deposit but does not reduce the Loan Amount. Because the Approved Project Budget allocates one hundred percent (100%) of Total Project Costs to the Loan and the Mezzanine Loan, an Equity Escrow Deposit that does not displace Loan proceeds has no effect on the Loan-to-Cost Ratio as defined above; it creates a corresponding surplus of sources over uses. Lender's credit approval contemplates that the escrowed equity will be applied to Project Costs ahead of Loan Advances; that result is achievable only if the Loan Amount is simultaneously reduced to $45,360,000 or Total Project Costs are restated upward. Borrower's and Lender's positions on the Loan Amount are reserved pending resolution. See Cover Memorandum, Issues 1 through 4.
:::

## 8.2 Loan-to-Value Ratio

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) The Loan-to-Value Ratio determined on an as-completed basis shall not exceed sixty-five percent (65%). **"Loan-to-Value Ratio"** or **"LTV"** means the ratio of the outstanding principal balance of the Loan to the appraised value of the Property on the applicable basis, as determined by an MAI appraisal conforming to the requirements of FIRREA and Lender's appraisal policy.

(b) As of the Closing Date, (i) the as-completed Loan-to-Value Ratio is $47,500,000 ÷ $72,800,000 = 65.25%, which exceeds the sixty-five percent (65%) maximum by $180,000 in principal amount ($72,800,000 × 65% = $47,320,000); and (ii) the as-stabilized Loan-to-Value Ratio is $47,500,000 ÷ $76,200,000 = 62.34%.

(c) Lender may obtain a new or updated appraisal at any time at Borrower's expense, and Borrower shall reimburse Lender for the cost thereof within ten (10) days after demand.

**Drafting Note:** The Term Sheet limits the as-completed Loan-to-Value Ratio to 65% (Sections 4 and 6.2). The Credit Memorandum applies a 70% policy limit and reports the as-completed ratio as a "Pass" at 65.25%. The executed Term Sheet governs as between the parties, so the Loan as sized exceeds the as-completed limit. The same $2,140,000 reduction that cures the Loan-to-Cost exceedance would also reduce the as-completed Loan-to-Value Ratio to 62.31% and the as-stabilized ratio to 59.53%. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 2.
:::

## 8.3 Debt Service Coverage Ratio

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) The DSCR shall not be less than 1.25x, tested (i) at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and (ii) annually thereafter, in each case based on the Net Operating Income for the most recent twelve (12) month period.

(b) **Cure.** If the DSCR is less than 1.25x at any test date, Borrower shall, at Lender's election exercised in writing within thirty (30) days after delivery of the applicable compliance certificate, either (i) make a principal curtailment sufficient to restore the DSCR to 1.25x, or (ii) deposit cash collateral in an amount determined by Lender sufficient to restore the DSCR to 1.25x. Any principal curtailment shall be accompanied by payment of the Exit Fee allocable to the amount curtailed.

(c) **Drafting Note.** The first test date precedes stabilization. Substantial Completion is projected for August 31, 2027, and stabilization (95% occupancy) is projected for approximately May 2028; the Mini-Perm Period commences August 29, 2027. A test based on trailing twelve-month actual Net Operating Income at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period would necessarily reflect a partially leased project and would be very likely to fail. Lender's practice is to test on a stabilized basis with a lease-up adjustment. Borrower and Lender must agree on the test basis. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 25.
:::

## 8.4 Debt Yield

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
The Debt Yield shall not be less than [eight and fifty hundredths percent (8.50%)], tested at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and annually thereafter. This covenant does not appear in the Term Sheet and is proposed by Lender to address the absence of any coverage test that measures the Loan against the Project's income capacity independently of the interest rate. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 25.
:::

## 8.5 Borrower Net Worth

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower shall maintain a minimum net worth of not less than $12,000,000, tested annually within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year, and certified in a compliance certificate. For purposes of this covenant, net worth shall be determined in accordance with GAAP.

**Drafting Note:** Borrower's asserted net worth of $14,200,000 cannot be reconciled to the balance sheet implicit in the record. Borrower's only identified asset is the Property, acquired for $8,200,000 and encumbered by the Prior Deed of Trust in the original principal amount of $3,400,000. That balance sheet would produce a net worth of approximately $4,800,000. Following closing, Borrower's assets and liabilities increase roughly dollar-for-dollar with Loan and Mezzanine Loan advances, so the covenant would not be cured by construction. The covenant as drafted would therefore be breached on the Closing Date unless the capital structure is restated or the covenant is redefined to permit add-backs for the Property at appraised value and for contributions. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 26.
:::

## 8.6 Guarantor Liquidity

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
The Guarantors shall maintain combined liquidity of not less than $5,000,000, tested quarterly within forty-five (45) days after the end of each calendar quarter and evidenced by current personal financial statements and supporting account statements. **"Liquidity"** means cash, Cash Equivalents and marketable securities readily convertible to cash within thirty (30) days, excluding any interest in Borrower, any Related Entity or the Project, and excluding any asset pledged to another lender.

As of the Closing Date, the Guarantors' combined liquidity is approximately $9,300,000 ($6,100,000 attributable to Elena Vasquez-Torres and $3,200,000 attributable to Reginald K. Osei), which satisfies the covenant with a cushion of approximately $4,300,000.
:::

## 8.7 Guarantor Net Worth

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Each Guarantor shall maintain a personal net worth of not less than [seventy-five percent (75%) of the net worth reflected in such Guarantor's most recent personal financial statement delivered to Lender], tested annually. As of the Closing Date, that threshold would be approximately $[22,350,000] for Elena Vasquez-Torres and $[8,625,000] for Reginald K. Osei. **Drafting Note:** The Term Sheet contains no Guarantor net worth covenant, although Section 15 of the Term Sheet lists as an Event of Default the failure of "any Guarantor's net worth" to satisfy "the minimum threshold set forth in Section 6.4" — a cross-reference to the Borrower's net worth covenant. Lender must either fix a Guarantor net worth threshold as proposed here or delete the corresponding Event of Default in Section 14.1. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 27.
:::

## 8.8 Testing Mechanics; Calculations; Adjustments

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) Each financial covenant shall be tested as of the last day of the applicable period and evidenced by a compliance certificate in the form of Exhibit I delivered within the time period specified in Exhibit F.

(b) Net Operating Income shall be determined on an actual basis for the trailing twelve (12) month period, and shall be annualized only if the Project has been in operation for fewer than twelve (12) months, in which case Net Operating Income shall be annualized by dividing the Net Operating Income for the period of operation by the number of months of operation and multiplying by twelve. Annualization shall not be permitted after the Project has been in operation for twelve (12) months.

(c) Excluded from Net Operating Income: (i) rent from any tenant that is more than sixty (60) days in arrears, (ii) rent from any tenant that is a Related Entity, (iii) any revenue from a unit or space that is not lawfully occupied (including any residential unit within or above the Environmental Restricted Area as to which a certificate of occupancy has not been issued), (iv) security deposits and non-recurring income, and (v) the amount of any CC&R assessment payable to the Brightleaf Historic District Association in excess of the amount reflected in Borrower's operating budget.

(d) In determining compliance, Lender may make adjustments for non-recurring items, above-market or below-market leases, and items that Lender reasonably determines do not reflect normalized operations.

**Drafting Note:** The Appraised Value and the Appraiser's projected Stabilized Net Operating Income of $4,876,800 do not include the annual assessment payable to the Brightleaf Historic District Association under the Declaration in Book 6984, Page 1155, which is $0.12 per square foot of gross building area, or approximately $34,500 per annum for 287,500 square feet. Adjusting Net Operating Income for that assessment reduces it to approximately $4,842,300, reduces the DSCR to approximately 1.30x and reduces the indicated as-stabilized value at the appraiser's 6.40% capitalization rate to approximately $75,660,900 (and the Loan-to-Value Ratio to approximately 62.78%). See Cover Memorandum, Issue 19.
:::

## 8.9 Covenant Compliance Certificate

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
With each compliance certificate, Borrower shall deliver a schedule showing the computation of each financial covenant in reasonable detail, and the calculation of Total Project Costs, outstanding Advances, Retainage held, the Interest Reserve Balance and the then-current DSCR and Debt Yield.
:::

Lender's credit approval contemplates that the escrowed equity will be applied to Project Costs ahead of Loan Advances; that result is achievable only if the Loan Amount is simultaneously reduced to $45,360,000 or Total Project Costs are restated upward. Borrower's and Lender's positions on the Loan Amount are reserved pending resolution. See Cover Memorandum, Issues 1 through 4.
:::

## 8.2 Loan-to-Value Ratio

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) The Loan-to-Value Ratio determined on an as-completed basis shall not exceed sixty-five percent (65%). **"Loan-to-Value Ratio"** or **"LTV"** means the ratio of the outstanding principal balance of the Loan to the appraised value of the Property on the applicable basis, as determined by an MAI appraisal conforming to the requirements of FIRREA and Lender's appraisal policy.

(b) As of the Closing Date, (i) the as-completed Loan-to-Value Ratio is $47,500,000 ÷ $72,800,000 = 65.25%, which exceeds the sixty-five percent (65%) maximum by $180,000 in principal amount ($72,800,000 × 65% = $47,320,000); and (ii) the as-stabilized Loan-to-Value Ratio is $47,500,000 ÷ $76,200,000 = 62.34%.

(c) Lender may obtain a new or updated appraisal at any time at Borrower's expense, and Borrower shall reimburse Lender for the cost thereof within ten (10) days after demand.

**Drafting Note:** The Term Sheet limits the as-completed Loan-to-Value Ratio to 65% (Sections 4 and 6.2). The Credit Memorandum applies a 70% policy limit and reports the as-completed ratio as a "Pass" at 65.25%. The executed Term Sheet governs as between the parties, so the Loan as sized exceeds the as-completed limit. The same $2,140,000 reduction that cures the Loan-to-Cost exceedance would also reduce the as-completed Loan-to-Value Ratio to 62.31% and the as-stabilized ratio to 59.53%. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 2.
:::

## 8.3 Debt Service Coverage Ratio

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) The DSCR shall not be less than 1.25x, tested (i) at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and (ii) annually thereafter, in each case based on the Net Operating Income for the most recent twelve (12) month period.

(b) **Cure.** If the DSCR is less than 1.25x at any test date, Borrower shall, at Lender's election exercised in writing within thirty (30) days after delivery of the applicable compliance certificate, either (i) make a principal curtailment sufficient to restore the DSCR to 1.25x, or (ii) deposit cash collateral in an amount determined by Lender sufficient to restore the DSCR to 1.25x. Any principal curtailment shall be accompanied by payment of the Exit Fee allocable to the amount curtailed.

(c) **Drafting Note.** The first test date precedes stabilization. Substantial Completion is projected for August 31, 2027, and stabilization (95% occupancy) is projected for approximately May 2028; the Mini-Perm Period commences August 29, 2027. A test based on trailing twelve-month actual Net Operating Income at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period would necessarily reflect a partially leased project and would be very likely to fail. Lender's practice is to test on a stabilized basis with a lease-up adjustment. Borrower and Lender must agree on the test basis. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 25.
:::

## 8.4 Debt Yield

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
The Debt Yield shall not be less than [eight and fifty hundredths percent (8.50%)], tested at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and annually thereafter. This covenant does not appear in the Term Sheet and is proposed by Lender to address the absence of any coverage test that measures the Loan against the Project's income capacity independently of the interest rate. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 25.
:::

## 8.5 Borrower Net Worth

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower shall maintain a minimum net worth of not less than $12,000,000, tested annually within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year, and certified in a compliance certificate. For purposes of this covenant, net worth shall be determined in accordance with GAAP.

**Drafting Note:** Borrower's asserted net worth of $14,200,000 cannot be reconciled to the balance sheet implicit in the record. Borrower's only identified asset is the Property, acquired for $8,200,000 and encumbered by the Prior Deed of Trust in the original principal amount of $3,400,000. That balance sheet would produce a net worth of approximately $4,800,000. Following closing, Borrower's assets and liabilities increase roughly dollar-for-dollar with Loan and Mezzanine Loan advances, so the covenant would not be cured by construction. The covenant as drafted would therefore be breached on the Closing Date unless the capital structure is restated or the covenant is redefined to permit add-backs for the Property at appraised value and for contributions. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 26.
:::

## 8.6 Guarantor Liquidity

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
The Guarantors shall maintain combined liquidity of not less than $5,000,000, tested quarterly within forty-five (45) days after the end of each calendar quarter and evidenced by current personal financial statements and supporting account statements. **"Liquidity"** means cash, Cash Equivalents and marketable securities readily convertible to cash within thirty (30) days, excluding any interest in Borrower, any Related Entity or the Project, and excluding any asset pledged to another lender.

As of the Closing Date, the Guarantors' combined liquidity is approximately $9,300,000 ($6,100,000 attributable to Elena Vasquez-Torres and $3,200,000 attributable to Reginald K. Osei), which satisfies the covenant with a cushion of approximately $4,300,000.
:::

## 8.7 Guarantor Net Worth

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Each Guarantor shall maintain a personal net worth of not less than [seventy-five percent (75%) of the net worth reflected in such Guarantor's most recent personal financial statement delivered to Lender], tested annually. As of the Closing Date, that threshold would be approximately $[22,350,000] for Elena Vasquez-Torres and $[8,625,000] for Reginald K. Osei. **Drafting Note:** The Term Sheet contains no Guarantor net worth covenant, although Section 15 of the Term Sheet lists as an Event of Default the failure of "any Guarantor's net worth" to satisfy "the minimum threshold set forth in Section 6.4" — a cross-reference to the Borrower's net worth covenant. Lender must either fix a Guarantor net worth threshold as proposed here or delete the corresponding Event of Default in Section 14.1. See Cover Memorandum, Issue 27.
:::

## 8.8 Testing Mechanics; Calculations; Adjustments

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) Each financial covenant shall be tested as of the last day of the applicable period and evidenced by a compliance certificate in the form of Exhibit I delivered within the time period specified in Exhibit F.

(b) Net Operating Income shall be determined on an actual basis for the trailing twelve (12) month period, and shall be annualized only if the Project has been in operation for fewer than twelve (12) months, in which case Net Operating Income shall be annualized by dividing the Net Operating Income for the period of operation by the number of months of operation and multiplying by twelve. Annualization shall not be permitted after the Project has been in operation for twelve (12) months.

(c) Excluded from Net Operating Income: (i) rent from any tenant that is more than sixty (60) days in arrears, (ii) rent from any tenant that is a Related Entity, (iii) any revenue from a unit or space that is not lawfully occupied (including any residential unit within or above the Environmental Restricted Area as to which a certificate of occupancy has not been issued), (iv) security deposits and non-recurring income, and (v) the amount of any CC&R assessment payable to the Brightleaf Historic District Association in excess of the amount reflected in Borrower's operating budget.

(d) In determining compliance, Lender may make adjustments for non-recurring items, above-market or below-market leases, and items that Lender reasonably determines do not reflect normalized operations.

**Drafting Note:** The Appraised Value and the Appraiser's projected Stabilized Net Operating Income of $4,876,800 do not include the annual assessment payable to the Brightleaf Historic District Association under the Declaration in Book 6984, Page 1155, which is $0.12 per square foot of gross building area, or approximately $34,500 per annum for 287,500 square feet. Adjusting Net Operating Income for that assessment reduces it to approximately $4,842,300, reduces the DSCR to approximately 1.30x and reduces the indicated as-stabilized value at the appraiser's 6.40% capitalization rate to approximately $75,660,900 (and the Loan-to-Value Ratio to approximately 62.78%). See Cover Memorandum, Issue 19.
:::

## 8.9 Covenant Compliance Certificate

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
With each compliance certificate, Borrower shall deliver a schedule showing the computation of each financial covenant in reasonable detail, and the calculation of Total Project Costs, outstanding Advances, Retainage held, the Interest Reserve Balance and the then-current DSCR and Debt Yield.
:::

# ARTICLE IX — SINGLE-PURPOSE ENTITY AND SEPARATENESS COVENANTS

:::

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) maintain its own books, records, financial statements, bank accounts and taxpayer identification number separate from those of any other Person;

(b) not commingle its funds or other assets with those of any member, Affiliate or other Person, and not maintain any joint or common account;

(c) hold itself out as a separate and distinct entity, conduct its business in its own name, and not hold itself out as being liable for the debts of any other Person or as having any obligation to satisfy the obligations of any other Person;

(d) observe all limited liability company formalities, including holding member and manager meetings as required by its Operating Agreement, maintaining minutes and records, and making all required filings with the North Carolina Secretary of State;

(e) pay its own liabilities and expenses from its own funds and allocate fairly and reasonably any overhead expenses shared with any Other Person (including shared office space, equipment and services), and maintain an arm's-length relationship with each Affiliate;

(f) not guarantee or otherwise become liable for the obligations of any member, Affiliate or other Person, and not pledge its assets for the benefit of any other Person;

(g) not make any loan or advance to any member, Affiliate or other Person, and not acquire any obligation of any member or Affiliate;

(h) not identify any member or Affiliate as a division or part of Borrower, and not use the stationery or business forms of any member or Affiliate;

(i) not enter into any transaction with any Affiliate except in compliance with Section 7.6;

(j) maintain adequate capital for the normal obligations reasonably foreseeable in a business of its size and character, and remain solvent;

(k) not engage in any transaction with any member or Affiliate that is not on arm's-length terms, and not take any action that would cause the separate identity of Borrower to be disregarded;

(l) not acquire obligations or securities of, or make any loans to, any member or Affiliate;

(m) conduct all dealings with third parties in its own name, and maintain a separate telephone number, address and (if applicable) website;

(n) not file any voluntary petition in bankruptcy, consent to the appointment of a receiver or trustee, make a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or admit in writing its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, without the prior unanimous written consent of all members and the affirmative vote of the Independent Manager; and

(o) cause the Related Entities not to (i) hold themselves out as having any liability for the debts of Borrower, (ii) commingle their funds with those of Borrower, (iii) file any involuntary petition in bankruptcy against Borrower, or (iv) take any action inconsistent with Borrower's separate existence.

# ARTICLE IX — SINGLE-PURPOSE ENTITY AND SEPARATENESS COVENANTS

## 9.1 Single-Purpose Entity Status

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower shall at all times maintain its status as a single-purpose entity and shall not engage in any business other than the acquisition, development, construction, ownership, leasing, management and operation of the Project.
:::

## 9.2 Separateness Covenants

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower shall, and shall cause the Related Entities to, observe each of the following:
:::

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) maintain its own books, records, financial statements, bank accounts and taxpayer identification number separate from those of any other Person;

(b) not commingle its funds or other assets with those of any member, Affiliate or other Person, and not maintain any joint or common account;

(c) hold itself out as a separate and distinct entity, conduct its business in its own name, and not hold itself out as being liable for the debts of any other Person or as having any obligation to satisfy the obligations of any other Person;

(d) observe all limited liability company formalities, including holding member and manager meetings as required by its Operating Agreement, maintaining minutes and records, and making all required filings with the North Carolina Secretary of State;

(e) pay its own liabilities and expenses from its own funds and allocate fairly and reasonably any overhead expenses shared with any Other Person (including shared office space, equipment and services), and maintain an arm's-length relationship with each Affiliate;

(f) not guarantee or otherwise become liable for the obligations of any member, Affiliate or other Person, and not pledge its assets for the benefit of any other Person;

(g) not make any loan or advance to any member, Affiliate or other Person, and not acquire any obligation of any member or Affiliate;

(h) not identify any member or Affiliate as a division or part of Borrower, and not use the stationery or business forms of any member or Affiliate;

(i) not enter into any transaction with any Affiliate except in compliance with Section 7.6;

(j) maintain adequate capital for the normal obligations reasonably foreseeable in a business of its size and character, and remain solvent;

(k) not engage in any transaction with any member or Affiliate that is not on arm's-length terms, and not take any action that would cause the separate identity of Borrower to be disregarded;

(l) not acquire obligations or securities of, or make any loans to, any member or Affiliate;

(m) conduct all dealings with third parties in its own name, and maintain a separate telephone number, address and (if applicable) website;

(n) not file any voluntary petition in bankruptcy, consent to the appointment of a receiver or trustee, make a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or admit in writing its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, without the prior unanimous written consent of all members and the affirmative vote of the Independent Manager; and

(o) cause the Related Entities not to (i) hold themselves out as having any liability for the debts of Borrower, (ii) commingle their funds with those of Borrower, (iii) file any involuntary petition in bankruptcy against Borrower, or (iv) take any action inconsistent with Borrower's separate existence.
:::

## 9.3 Independent Manager

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower shall maintain at all times at least one (1) natural person as an Independent Manager who (a) is not, and has not been within five (5) years, an officer, director, manager, employee, member, creditor, supplier, customer, attorney, accountant or Affiliate of Borrower, any member of Borrower, the Mezzanine Lender, Thomas R. Chen or any Related Entity, (b) has no economic interest in Borrower or any Related Entity, and (c) is not a party to any agreement with Borrower or any Related Entity that would compromise such person's independence. :::

# ARTICLE X — ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS

## 10.1 Acknowledgement of Environmental Condition

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower acknowledges that (a) the Phase I ESA identified one Recognized Environmental Condition at the Property, consisting of residual petroleum contamination from a former 2,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank located in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102; (b) remediation consisting of excavation and off-site disposal of impacted soil was completed in September 2024; (c) residual contamination remains in place in the Environmental Restricted Area at concentrations exceeding NCDEQ residential Preliminary Soil Remediation Goals for TPH-DRO and benzene in soil, and benzene in soil gas exceeds NCDEQ residential vapor intrusion screening levels; and (d) the NFA Letter is conditional, and the Property is not a "clean closure" site.
:::

## 10.2 Compliance with the NFA Letter

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower shall comply with each condition of the NFA Letter, including:
:::

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) **Vapor Mitigation System.** Design, install, commission, operate and maintain a passive sub-slab depressurization system with conversion capability to active depressurization (the **"Vapor Mitigation System"**) beneath each enclosed structure constructed within or over the Environmental Restricted Area, in accordance with the NFA Letter, the guidelines of the NCDEQ Division of Waste Management and the design of a professional engineer licensed in North Carolina. Borrower shall deliver to Lender and to NCDEQ as-built drawings and a system performance verification report within ninety (90) days after completion of the building foundation in the affected area, and shall deliver a copy of the system's operating and maintenance manual to Lender.

(b) **Land Use Restriction.** Restrict the Environmental Restricted Area to non-residential use, and not construct, occupy, lease or permit the occupancy of any residential unit or other sensitive use within or above the Environmental Restricted Area unless and until the NFA Letter is modified in accordance with Section 10.4.

(c) **Soil Management Plan.** Submit a soil management plan to NCDEQ for approval, and comply with it, prior to any excavation, grading or other subsurface disturbance within the Environmental Restricted Area. Borrower shall cause the Soil Management Plan to be incorporated into the Construction Documents and delivered to the General Contractor and each subcontractor performing work in the affected area.

(d) **Deed Notice.** Record, and maintain of record, a deed notice in the Durham County Registry of Deeds in the form required by the NFA Letter, describing the Environmental Restricted Area by metes and bounds (or by reference to a recorded plat), the nature and extent of residual contamination, and the non-residential use restriction. Borrower shall deliver to Lender a recorded copy, together with evidence of the recording date, promptly following recording.

(e) **Reporting.** Deliver to Lender, within ten (10) Business Days after delivery or receipt, copies of all correspondence, submissions, approvals, notices and reports exchanged with NCDEQ relating to the Property, and annual certifications of continued compliance with each condition of the NFA Letter.
:::

## 10.3 No Reopening; No Adverse Modification

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower shall not take, and shall not permit any tenant or contractor to take, any action that would cause NCDEQ to reopen the regulatory file for Site ID IHSB-24-1203, revoke or modify the NFA Letter adversely, or require additional investigation or remediation, including any change in land use, any unpermitted subsurface disturbance, or any failure to maintain the Vapor Mitigation System.
:::

## 10.4 Modification of the NFA Letter

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Borrower may seek a modification of the NFA Letter to permit residential use of the Environmental Restricted Area only with Lender's prior written consent (which may be conditioned on Lender's review and approval of the proposed scope of work, the additional investigation and risk assessment, the engineering controls and the cost thereof). Borrower shall bear all costs of any such modification and shall deposit the amount of any additional cost with Lender before it is incurred. No modification shall be deemed effective for purposes of Section 10.2(b) until NCDEQ has issued a written modification and Borrower has delivered a copy to Lender.
:::

## 10.5 Environmental Indemnity; Pollution Legal Liability Insurance

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}

:::

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}

# ARTICLE XIV — EVENTS OF DEFAULT

## 14.1 Events of Default

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Each of the following shall constitute an **"Event of Default"** under this Agreement and the other Loan Documents:
:::

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
(a) **Payment.** Borrower fails to pay any principal, interest, Fee or other amount due under any Loan Document when due, and such failure continues for five (5) days after the due date.

(b) **Interest Reserve Deficiency.** Borrower fails to fund any deposit required by Section 4.5(e) within five (5) Business Days after written notice.

(c) **Representations.** Any representation or warranty made by Borrower or any Guarantor in any Loan Document or in any certificate delivered thereunder proves to have been false or misleading in any material respect when made or deemed made.

(d) **Covenants (Non-Monetary).** Borrower fails to observe or perform any covenant or agreement contained in any Loan Document (other than a covenant described in another clause of this Section) and such failure continues for thirty (30) days after the earlier of (i) written notice from Lender and (ii) the date Borrower knew or reasonably should have known of the failure; provided that if such failure is capable of cure but cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days and Borrower is diligently pursuing cure, the cure period shall be extended by an additional thirty (30) days.

(e) **Specified Covenants Not Subject to Cure.** Borrower breaches any covenant in Section 4.5(f), Article IX, Article X, Section 6.11, Article VII or Article VIII, and, in the case of a breach of Article VIII, such breach continues for thirty (30) days after Lender's written notice.

(f) **Voluntary Bankruptcy.** Borrower, any Guarantor or any member of Borrower commences any case, proceeding or other action under any bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, receivership or similar law, consents to the appointment of a receiver or trustee, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or admits in writing its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due.

(g) **Involuntary Bankruptcy.** Any case, proceeding or other action is commenced against Borrower, any Guarantor or any member of Borrower seeking to have an order for relief entered or seeking reorganization, liquidation or appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian, and such case is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

import sys
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

def set_cell_border(cell, sz=4, color="808080"):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    borders = tcPr.find(qn('w:tcBorders'))
    if borders is None:
        borders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(borders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right'):
        el = borders.find(qn('w:'+edge))
        if el is None:
            el = OxmlElement('w:'+edge); borders.append(el)
        el.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'),str(sz))
        el.set(qn('w:space'),'0'); el.set(qn('w:color'),color)

def shade(cell, fill="DCE4EE"):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    sh = OxmlElement('w:shd'); sh.set(qn('w:val'),'clear'); sh.set(qn('w:color'),'auto'); sh.set(qn('w:fill'),fill)
    tcPr.append(sh)

def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); el.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(el)

def cant_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); el.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(el)

def fmt_tables(doc):
    for t in doc.tables:
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        tblPr = t._tbl.tblPr
        # cell margins
        mar = OxmlElement('w:tblCellMar')
        for side,val in (('top',40),('bottom',40),('left',80),('right',80)):
            e = OxmlElement('w:'+side); e.set(qn('w:w'),str(val)); e.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa'); mar.append(e)
        tblPr.append(mar)
        for i,row in enumerate(t.rows):
            cant_split(row)
            if i==0: repeat_header(row)
            for j,cell in enumerate(row.cells):
                set_cell_border(cell)
                if i==0: shade(cell)
                for p in cell.paragraphs:
                    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
                    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(1)
                    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
                    if i==0:
                        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
                    for r in p.runs:
                        r.font.size = Pt(8.5)
                        r.font.name='Times New Roman'
                        if i==0: r.font.bold = True

def add_running_header(doc, left_text, right_text):
    for sec in doc.sections:
        hdr = sec.header
        hdr.is_linked_to_previous = False
        p = hdr.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = ""

def set_cell_border(cell, sz=4, color="808080"):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    borders = tcPr.find(qn('w:tcBorders'))
    if borders is None:
        borders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(borders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right'):
        el = borders.find(qn('w:'+edge))
        if el is None:
            el = OxmlElement('w:'+edge); borders.append(el)
        el.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'),str(sz))

def shade(cell, fill="DCE4EE"):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    sh = OxmlElement('w:shd'); sh.set(qn('w:val'),'clear'); sh.set(qn('w:color'),'auto'); sh.set(qn('w:fill'),fill)
    tcPr.append(sh)

def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); el.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(el)

def cant_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); el.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(el)

def fmt_tables(doc):

        for side,val in (('top',40),('bottom',40),('left',80),('right',80)):

        tblPr.append(mar)
        for i,row in enumerate(t.rows):
            cant_split(row)

{"command": "cd "$WORKSPACE_DIR" && cat > work/post.py <<'PY'
import sys, re
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

TOTAL_TWIPS = 9360  # 6.5 inches usable width

def set_cell_border(cell, sz=4, color="8C9AAB"):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    borders = tcPr.find(qn('w:tcBorders'))
    if borders is None:
        borders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.insert(0, borders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right'):
        el = borders.find(qn('w:'+edge))
        if el is None:
            el = OxmlElement('w:'+edge); borders.append(el)
        el.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'),str(sz))
        el.set(qn('w:space'),'0'); el.set(qn('w:color'),color)

def shade(cell, fill="DCE4EE"):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    sh = OxmlElement('w:shd'); sh.set(qn('w:val'),'clear'); sh.set(qn('w:color'),'auto'); sh.set(qn('w:fill'),fill)
    tcPr.append(sh)

def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); el.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(el)

def cant_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); el.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(el)

def col_weights(table):
    ncols = len(table.columns)
    weights = []
    for c in range(ncols):
        best = 6
        for row in table.rows:
            cells = row.cells
            if c < len(cells):
                txt = cells[c].text.strip()
                # longest unbreakable-ish measure: chars, but long words penalised less
                best = max(best, min(len(txt), 70))
        weights.append(best)
    # dampen extremes
    weights = [w ** 0.85 for w in weights]
    return weights

def apply_widths(table):
    ncols = len(table.columns)
    w = col_weights(table)
    tot = sum(w)
    widths = [max(600, int(TOTAL_TWIPS * x / tot)) for x in w]
    # renormalise after clamping
    diff = TOTAL_TWIPS - sum(widths)
    idx = widths.index(max(widths))
    widths[idx] += diff
    tbl = table._tbl
    # tblW
    tblPr = tbl.tblPr
    for el in tblPr.findall(qn('w:tblW')):
        tblPr.remove(el)
    tw = OxmlElement('w:tblW'); tw.set(qn('w:w'), str(TOTAL_TWIPS)); tw.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa'); tblPr.append(tw)
    lay = OxmlElement('w:tblLayout'); lay.set(qn('w:type'),'fixed'); tblPr.append(lay)
    # grid
    grid = tbl.find(qn('w:tblGrid'))
    if grid is not None:
        for gc in list(grid):
            grid.remove(gc)
        for width in widths:
            gc = OxmlElement('w:gridCol'); gc.set(qn('w:w'), str(width)); grid.append(gc)
    for row in table.rows:
        for j, cell in enumerate(row.cells):
            tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
            for el in tcPr.findall(qn('w:tcW')):
                tcPr.remove(el)
            tcw = OxmlElement('w:tcW'); tcw.set(qn('w:w'), str(widths[j])); tcw.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa')
            tcPr.insert(0, tcw)

def fmt_tables(doc):
    for t in doc.tables:
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        t.autofit = False
        apply_widths(t)
        tblPr = t._tbl.tblPr
        mar = OxmlElement('w:tblCellMar')
        for side,val in (('top',40),('bottom',40),('left',80),('right',80)):
            e = OxmlElement('w:'+side); e.set(qn('w:w'),str(val)); e.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa'); mar.append(e)
        tblPr.append(mar)
        for i,row in enumerate(t.rows):
            cant_split(row)
            if i==0: repeat_header(row)
            for j,cell in enumerate(row.cells):
                set_cell_border(cell)
                if i==0: shade(cell)
                for p in cell.paragraphs:
                    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
                    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(1)
                    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
                    if i==0:
                        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
                    for r in p.runs:
                        r.font.size = Pt(8)
                        r.font.name='Times New Roman'
                        if i==0: r.font.bold = True
        # keep table with preceding heading
        # add small spacer after table
        p = OxmlElement('w:p')
        t._tbl.addnext(p)

def add_running_header(doc, right_text):
    for sec in doc.sections:
        hdr = sec.header
        hdr.is_linked_to_previous = False
        p = hdr.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = ""
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
        r = p.add_run(right_text)
        r.font.size = Pt(7.5); r.font.name='Times New Roman'; r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x66,0x66,0x66)
        pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
        pbdr = OxmlElement('w:pBdr'); b = OxmlElement('w:bottom')
        b.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); b.set(qn('w:sz'),'4'); b.set(qn('w:space'),'2'); b.set(qn('w:color'),'AAAAAA')
        pbdr.append(b); pPr.append(pbdr)

src, dst, header_text = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
doc = Document(src)
fmt_tables(doc)
add_running_header(doc, header_text)
doc.save(dst)
print("ok", dst, "tables:", len(doc.tables))
PY

## 3. Executive Summary

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
The Loan can be documented, but the record as furnished does not support several of the conclusions the Credit Memorandum relies on, and three of those conclusions go to the core of the credit rather than to documentation niceties. They are:

**(a) The Project has no borrower equity, and the Loan is oversized against the Bank's own limits.** The sources and uses allocates one hundred percent of the $56,700,000 of Total Project Costs to the $47,500,000 senior loan and the $9,200,000 mezzanine loan, with Borrower cash equity stated at **$0** (Draw Schedule, "Summary" and "Detailed Budget" worksheets; Credit Memorandum §5.1 and Appendix C). The $8,200,000 land cost is shown in the Detailed Budget as funded by **Mezzanine Loan proceeds**, not by member equity. That is irreconcilable with the Term Sheet (§5.2: land "funded from prior capital contributions by the Borrower's members"), the Credit Memorandum (§2.2: "capital calls from all three members"), and the Organizational Chart (§1.3: contributed by Ms. Vasquez-Torres "from her personal resources"). On the face of the sources and uses, the Mezzanine Loan is a land take-out: at closing it repays whoever funded the land. If that is right, then the "land equity" that the Credit Memorandum credits at $8,200,000 in its equity analysis (Credit Memorandum §5.3, §9.1: \\$2,140,000 cash + \\$8,200,000 land = \\$10,340,000, or 18.2%) is the same $8,200,000 that the Credit Memorandum's own sources table has already counted as mezzanine debt. It is counted twice. True equity is $0, or $2,140,000 if the equity escrow is funded with genuinely independent cash. See Issue 5.

**(b) The Loan exceeds both of the Bank's leverage limits as set in the executed Term Sheet, and the prescribed cure does not work.** Loan-to-cost is 83.77% against an 80% maximum (a $2,140,000 excess). As-completed loan-to-value is 65.25% against the 65% maximum in Term Sheet §§ 4 and 6.2 (a $180,000 excess) — a breach the Credit Memorandum does not report, because it measures against a 70% policy limit that contradicts the executed Term Sheet. The Credit Memorandum's cure — deposit $2,140,000 of equity — is presented as an alternative to reducing the Loan Amount, but on its own it cannot work: because every dollar of Total Project Costs is already allocated to the two loans, adding $2,140,000 of equity to the sources column while leaving the Loan at $47,500,000 produces $58,840,000 of sources against $56,700,000 of uses. The equity must **displace** Loan proceeds. The two "alternatives" in Credit Memorandum §5.1 and §10.1.2 are in fact two halves of a single fix: reduce the Loan Amount to $45,360,000 **and** fund $2,140,000 of equity. See Issues 1, 2 and 3.

**(c) The interest reserve is not adequate, and the record gives three different answers to how inadequate.** The Draw Schedule projects a **surplus** of $221,325 on a Daily Simple SOFR assumption of 3.50%; the same worksheet's own sensitivity table at 4.35% projects a **shortfall** of $(365,830); and the Credit Memorandum projects a shortfall of $(565,000). All three purport to measure the same thing. The difference is methodology: the Draw Schedule's month-by-month accrual is arithmetically sound but is built on a rate assumption 85 basis points below the rate used everywhere else in the record, and the Credit Memorandum's average-balance shortcut overstates total interest by roughly $200,000 at the same rate. On the Draw Schedule's own draw pattern at 4.35% Daily Simple SOFR, total construction-period interest is approximately $5,211,500 and the shortfall is approximately $361,500. The reserve is short, and the Senior Loan Committee approved it as "adequate." See Issues 9 and 10.
:::

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}

- **The Draw Schedule does not foot.** Draw 9 shows $4,275,000 of components against a stated draw of $3,275,000, and the component columns aggregate to $48,500,000 against a $47,500,000 facility. The Detailed Budget's "Net Disbursable" total is overstated by $725,000. The 10% retainage is $3,475,000, but the documents release $3,275,000. See Issues 11, 12 and 13.
- **The environmental record is materially incomplete.** The NFA letter requires a deed notice to be recorded by **November 29, 2024**. The Phase I ESA (October 28, 2024) records no evidence of recording. The Appraisal (November 15, 2024) states it **is** recorded. The Title Commitment (effective December 5, 2024) searches the public records and **does not show it**. It is also absent from the Term Sheet's list of Permitted Exceptions. If the notice was not recorded, the NFA determination is out of compliance and the site's regulatory status is impaired; if it was recorded, the Title Policy will carry an unlisted exception. Either way the Bank needs the recorded instrument. The Phase II report and the NFA letter are not in the record at all. See Issues 21, 23 and 27.
- **The residential use restriction has not been resolved and the record does not establish its scope.** The Credit Memorandum asserts that fourteen residential units sit above the restricted 0.38 acres. The Phase I ESA expressly says that this "requires a detailed overlay" and was **not** determined. The number fourteen appears to have been taken from the unit count of three-bedroom units. The Appraisal expressly declines to adjust value for the restriction. See Issue 24.

Draw 8 is scheduled in the thirty-month of a thirty-month construction period and Draw 9 falls after maturity. See Issue 28.
- **Borrower's net worth cannot be reconciled and the covenant would be breached on day one.** Borrower's only identified asset is the Property, acquired for $8,200,000, encumbered by a $3,400,000 deed of trust. That balance sheet yields net worth of approximately **$4,800,000**, not the $14,200,000 asserted, and the proposed $12,000,000 covenant would fail immediately. See Issue 31.

The difference is methodology: the Draw Schedule's month-by-month accrual is arithmetically sound but is built on a rate assumption 85 basis points below the rate used everywhere else in the record, and the Credit Memorandum's average-balance shortcut overstates total interest by roughly $200,000 at the same rate. On the Draw Schedule's own draw pattern at 4.35% Daily Simple SOFR, total construction-period interest is approximately $5,211,500 and the shortfall is approximately $361,500. The reserve is short, and the Senior Loan Committee approved it as "adequate." See Issues 9 and 10.
:::

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Beyond those three, the record contains a cluster of issues that individually are capable of resolution but collectively indicate that the transaction documents were assembled from inconsistent inputs:

- **The Draw Schedule does not foot.** Draw 9 shows $4,275,000 of components against a stated draw of $3,275,000, and the component columns aggregate to $48,500,000 against a $47,500,000 facility. The Detailed Budget's "Net Disbursable" total is overstated by $725,000. The 10% retainage is $3,475,000, but the documents release $3,275,000. See Issues 11, 12 and 13.
- **The environmental record is materially incomplete.** The NFA letter requires a deed notice to be recorded by **November 29, 2024**. The Phase I ESA (October 28, 2024) records no evidence of recording. The Appraisal (November 15, 2024) states it **is** recorded. The Title Commitment (effective December 5, 2024) searches the public records and **does not show it**. It is also absent from the Term Sheet's list of Permitted Exceptions. If the notice was not recorded, the NFA determination is out of compliance and the site's regulatory status is impaired; if it was recorded, the Title Policy will carry an unlisted exception. Either way the Bank needs the recorded instrument. The Phase II report and the NFA letter are not in the record at all. See Issues 21, 23 and 27.
- **The residential use restriction has not been resolved and the record does not establish its scope.** The Credit Memorandum asserts that fourteen residential units sit above the restricted 0.38 acres. The Phase I ESA expressly says that this "requires a detailed overlay" and was **not** determined. The number fourteen appears to have been taken from the unit count of three-bedroom units. The Appraisal expressly declines to adjust value for the restriction. See Issue 24.
- **Two dates are three days apart and cannot both be met.** Projected Substantial Completion is August 31, 2027; the Construction Maturity Date and the guaranteed completion date are August 28, 2027. Draw 8 is scheduled in the thirty-month of a thirty-month construction period and Draw 9 falls after maturity. See Issue 28.
- **Borrower's net worth cannot be reconciled and the covenant would be breached on day one.** Borrower's only identified asset is the Property, acquired for $8,200,000, encumbered by a $3,400,000 deed of trust. That balance sheet yields net worth of approximately **$4,800,000**, not the $14,200,000 asserted, and the proposed $12,000,000 covenant would fail immediately. See Issue 31.
:::

## 5. Schedule of Material Issues

::: {custom-style="Body Text"}
Each issue below states the sources, our finding (with arithmetic where the issue is quantitative), our recommendation, and the place in the Draft where the point is addressed. Where the record is silent we say so; we have not supplied facts the documents do not contain.
:::

## Part A — Capital Structure and Loan Sizing

### Issue 1 — Loan-to-Cost Ratio Exceeds the 80% Maximum, and the Prescribed Equity Escrow Does Not Cure It

**Severity: Critical.**

**Sources:** Term Sheet § 3.1 ($47,500,000), § 5.2 (Total Uses $56,700,000), § 6.1 (maximum LTC 80%); Credit Memorandum §§ 5.1, 5.3, 9.1, 10.1.2, 14.1; Draw Schedule, "Summary" worksheet (LTC Excess / Equity Shortfall $2,140,000).

**Finding.** The arithmetic is right and the conclusion is wrong. Loan-to-cost is $47,500,000 ÷ $56,700,000 = **83.7743%**, which exceeds the 80% maximum set in Term Sheet § 6.1. At 80%, the maximum senior loan is $56,700,000 × 0.80 = **$45,360,000**; the Loan exceeds that by **$2,140,000**. To restore 80%, either the Loan must come down or Total Project Costs must rise by $2,675,000 ($47,500,000 ÷ 0.80 = $59,375,000).

The Credit Memorandum's cure — deposit $2,140,000 into a Bank-controlled equity escrow — does not by itself change the ratio. Because the sources and uses allocates 100% of the $56,700,000 to the two loans (senior $47,500,000 = 83.77%; mezzanine $9,200,000 = 16.23%; Borrower cash equity **$0.00%**; Credit Memorandum § 5.1 and Appendix C; Draw Schedule "Summary"), there is no unfunded line item for the escrowed equity to pay. Adding $2,140,000 to sources produces $58,840,000 of sources against $56,700,000 of uses — a $2,140,000 surplus — while the Loan remains $47,500,000 and is still fully drawn to complete the Project. The escrowed cash does not reduce the numerator unless it reduces the commitment.

The Credit Memorandum presents the equity escrow (condition 10.1.2), a reduction of the Loan to $45,360,000, and additional evidence of independent land equity as **alternatives** ("either: (a) ... or (b) ... or (c) ..."). They are not alternatives. Option (a) requires option (b) to have any effect on LTC.

**Recommendation.** Treat the two as a single fix: reduce the Loan Amount to **$45,360,000** and require the **$2,140,000** equity contribution. That closes: $45,360,000 senior + $9,200,000 mezzanine + $2,140,000 equity = $56,700,000. LTC becomes exactly 80.00%. Obtain the Senior Loan Committee's written confirmation that the commitment is reduced (this is a change to the credit approval and to the Term Sheet loan amount, so it requires Committee action, not merely documentation). Alternatives worth presenting to the Bank: (i) restate Total Project Costs upward by adding the omitted costs in Issue 8 — note that adding the Triangle Commercial Bank payoff alone at its $3,400,000 original principal would bring Total Project Costs to $60,100,000 and LTC to 79.03%, but would require $3,400,000 of new funding (the same circularity); or (ii) substitute the Appraisal's $8,900,000 land value for the $8,200,000 cost basis in the budget, giving Total Project Costs of $57,400,000 and LTC of 82.75% — still above 80%. Neither alternative works without new equity.

**Draft reference:** § 8.1 (testing language and the arithmetic), § 3.1(g) (equity escrow condition with the reservation noted).

### Issue 2 — The As-Completed Loan-to-Value Ratio Exceeds the Executed Term Sheet's 65% Limit

**Severity: Critical.**

**Sources:** Term Sheet § 4 ("The Lender's maximum loan-to-value ratio shall not exceed 65% on an as-completed basis") and § 6.2 (65% as-completed and as-stabilized); Credit Memorandum § 6.1 and § 12 (maximum LTV 70% for construction loans; as-completed 65.25% reported as "Pass"); Appraisal § 10 ($72,800,000 as-completed; $76,200,000 as-stabilized; LTV 65.25% and 62.34%).

**Finding.** $47,500,000 ÷ $72,800,000 = **65.2473%**. That exceeds the Term Sheet's 65% cap by 0.25 percentage points, or **$180,000** in principal amount ($72,800,000 × 0.65 = $47,320,000). The as-stabilized ratio ($47,500,000 ÷ $76,200,000 = 62.3360%) is compliant.

The Credit Memorandum does not report this. Its underwriting table (¶ 6.1) and its regulatory section (¶ 12) both state the applicable maximum as **70%**, described as "Bank Policy," and mark the ratio as a pass. The executed Term Sheet says 65%, twice. The executed Term Sheet is the operative commercial agreement; a policy maximum more permissive than the deal-specific maximum does not override it. The credit file should be corrected so that the Committee approved against the limit the term sheet actually contains.

**Recommendation.** The Issue 1 fix cures this as well: at $45,360,000, the as-completed ratio is 62.31% and the as-stabilized ratio is 59.53%. Conform the covenant in the Loan Agreement to **65%** (not 70%). Ask the Bank to correct the credit file and to confirm the 70% figure was not the basis of approval.

**Draft reference:** § 8.2 (both limits stated as 65%, with the computation and the conflict disclosed).

### Issue 3 — Recommended Restructure and Loan Sizing

**Severity: Critical (structuring).**

**Sources:** All of the above; Credit Memorandum §§ 5.1, 5.3, 9.1, 12.

**Finding.** The record supports four internally consistent structures. We recommend the first.

| | Structure | Senior loan | Mezzanine | True equity | LTC | LTV (as-completed) | HVCRE |
|:--|:----------|------------:|----------:|------------:|----:|-------------------:|:------|
| A | **As documented** | $47,500,000 | $9,200,000 | $0 | 83.77% | 65.25% | Yes (14.20%) |
| B | **Credit Memorandum's escrow option taken alone** | $47,500,000 | $9,200,000 | $2,140,000 (unallocated) | 83.77% | 65.25% | Yes (14.20%) |
| C | **Recommended: loan reduction + equity** | $45,360,000 | $9,200,000 | $2,140,000 | 80.00% | 62.31% | Yes (14.20%) |
| D | **Loan reduction + equity + land at appraised value** | $45,360,000 | $9,200,000 | $2,140,000 (land booked at $8,900,000) | 80.00% | 62.31% | Borderline (15.16%) |

**Recommendation.** Adopt Structure C and offer Structure D to the Bank as a means of addressing the regulatory capital issue in Issue 4. In each case obtain: (i) Senior Loan Committee approval of the reduced commitment; (ii) a revised Term Sheet or written confirmation of the reduced Loan Amount so that the Loan Documents and the Term Sheet agree; (iii) a source-of-funds certification for the $2,140,000 (Issue 5); and (iv) restated sources and uses. Note that any reduction in the Loan Amount reduces the Origination Fee ($475,000 → $453,600 at 1.00%) and the available Interest Reserve, and that the Draw Schedule in Exhibit C of the Draft must then be re-based — we have not attempted that adjustment because the Draw Schedule needs to be rebuilt in any event (Issue 11).

**Draft reference:** § 8.1, § 8.2, § 3.1(g).

### Issue 4 — HVCRE Classification

**Severity: Medium.**

**Sources:** Credit Memorandum § 12; Appraisal § 10 (as-completed value $72,800,000); Draw Schedule (land at $8,200,000, no borrower equity).

**Finding.** The Credit Memorandum computes contributed capital as $2,140,000 equity plus $8,200,000 land at cost = $10,340,000, or **14.2033%** of the $72,800,000 as-completed value, against the 15% threshold ($10,920,000), a $580,000 shortfall. We reproduce those figures. Two observations. First, the calculation only reaches 14.2% because the Credit Memorandum credits the land at $8,200,000; on the sources and uses as actually constructed, the land is funded by the Mezzanine Loan and contributed capital would be **$2,140,000, or 2.94%** (Issue 5). Second, if the land is contributed at its **appraised** value of $8,900,000, contributed capital is $8,900,000 + $2,140,000 = $11,040,000, or **15.16%** — which would avoid HVCRE classification and the 150% risk weight, with no additional cash from the sponsor.

**Recommendation.** Present Structure D (Issue 3) to the Bank. Contributing the land at appraised value is the cheapest available route to the 15% threshold and is a matter of how the contribution is documented and evidenced, not of new money. Confirm with the Bank's regulatory reporting group that the land may be counted at appraised value under the applicable rule before the credit file is finalized.

**Draft reference:** § 8.1 (drafting note), § 5.4 (capital contribution schedule).

### Issue 5 — The Record Gives Three Irreconcilable Accounts of How the $8,200,000 Land Cost Was Funded; There Is No Borrower Equity

**Severity: Critical.**

**Sources:** Term Sheet § 5.2 ("The land ... was acquired by the Borrower prior to the closing of the Loan and is contributed to the Project as the Borrower's equity. The land acquisition was funded from prior capital contributions by the Borrower's members"); Credit Memorandum § 2.2 ("acquired by Ms. Vasquez-Torres on behalf of the Borrower through capital calls from all three members, including Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, at a total acquisition cost of $8,200,000"); Organizational Chart § 1.3 (land "contributed to Harborview Capital Partners LLC by Elena Vasquez-Torres at a cost basis of $8,200,000 ... originally acquired by Ms. Vasquez-Torres in a transaction funded from her personal resources"; Brightleaf Investors Group LLC and Mr. Osei each contributed **$0**); Draw Schedule, "Detailed Budget" line 1.01 (Land Acquisition — Vendor "Prior Acquisition — Closed"; Funded by Senior Loan **$0**; Funded by Mezzanine Loan **$8,200,000**; Funded by Borrower Equity **$0**; note: "Previously closed; funded by mezzanine loan proceeds and member capital calls"); Title Commitment Schedule A ¶ 5 (title vested by Special Warranty Deed recorded in Book 7598, Page 443 (Parcel 1) and Page 445 (Parcel 2), dated June 12, 2023, from Foster Street Properties LLC).

**Finding.** Three accounts, each inconsistent with the others and with the record evidence:

1. **Member capital contributions** (Term Sheet; Credit Memorandum — "all three members, including Brightleaf Investors Group LLC").
2. **Ms. Vasquez-Torres's personal resources** (Organizational Chart; Brightleaf Investors Group LLC and Mr. Osei each at $0).
3. **Mezzanine Loan proceeds** (Draw Schedule Detailed Budget — the only place in the record that states a funding source for the land, and it states a lender source, not an equity source).

The recorded deed supports none of the equity accounts in the form given: it shows a **purchase by Harborview directly from Foster Street Properties LLC on June 12, 2023** — not a contribution of land to a newly formed entity, and not a purchase by Ms. Vasquez-Torres. The Organizational Chart's statement that the land was contributed "upon formation of the project entity" is inconsistent with a formation date of March 14, 2019 and an acquisition date of June 12, 2023.

The accounts also conflict on the acquisition **date**: the Phase I ESA says Harborview "acquired the Subject Property in 2022" (§ 2.2); the Appraisal says the $8,200,000 was "the price paid by Harborview Capital Partners LLC in early 2024" (§ 6.1); the deed says June 12, 2023.

The consequence is not semantic. If the land was acquired in 2023 with member money and is refinanced at closing with Mezzanine Loan proceeds, then at closing the sponsor is repaid $8,200,000 (less the Prior Deed of Trust payoff) and the Project ends with **no equity at all**. The Credit Memorandum would then have double-counted the land: once as a use funded by mezzanine debt in its sources and uses, and again as $8,200,000 of "land equity" in its equity analysis (§ 5.3, § 9.1) and in its HVCRE analysis (§ 12). That is the single most important finding in this review, and it is the reason the LTC, LTV and HVCRE conclusions in the Credit Memorandum cannot be relied on.

**Recommendation.** Before the Draft is circulated, require from Borrower (and from Borrower's counsel) a **schedule of all capital contributions and member advances since formation**, on a cash-movement basis, identifying for each: date, amount, contributor, bank account, and the use to which the funds were applied; together with the settlement statement for the June 2023 acquisition, the source of the $8,200,000 purchase price (including the extent to which the Prior Deed of Trust was assumed rather than paid), and a certification that no member advance will be repaid from the proceeds of the Loan or the Mezzanine Loan. Verify the cash movements against bank statements, not just against a schedule. Then restate the sources and uses so that equity and debt are each shown once, and present the restated table to the Committee. If the Mezzanine Loan does reimburse member advances at closing, that is a **Distribution** of loan proceeds to the sponsor on day one; it must be identified as such, approved explicitly, and carved out of (or, better, prohibited by) the negative covenant. The Draft prohibits it absent express permission (§ 7.5(d)) and requires the Disclosure Schedule (§ 5.4) — but the prohibition is only as good as the disclosure behind it.

**Draft reference:** § 5.4 and Schedule 5.4; § 7.5(d); § 5.11; § 2.3; § 3.1(g).

### Issue 6 — Mezzanine Debt Service Is Not Funded Anywhere, and Combined Debt Service Coverage Is 0.93x

**Severity: High.**

**Sources:** Term Sheet § 1.4 (Mezzanine Loan $9,200,000, 12.50% fixed, coterminous); Credit Memorandum § 4.4 (interest "accrues and is paid-in-kind during construction; cash pay during mini-perm"); Draw Schedule Detailed Budget (no line item for mezzanine interest); Appraisal § 7 (Stabilized NOI $4,876,800); Credit Memorandum § 6.1 (DSCR 1.31x, senior only).

**Finding.** No document in the record funds Mezzanine Loan debt service. The Approved Project Budget of $56,700,000 contains no line for mezzanine interest, in either its PIK or its cash-pay form. At 12.50% on $9,200,000:

- PIK accretion over a 30-month Construction Period: $9,200,000 × 12.50% × 2.5 = **$2,875,000**, producing an accreted balance of approximately **$12,075,000** at the start of the Mini-Perm Period.
- Cash interest during the 12-month Mini-Perm Period on that balance: **$1,509,375**.
- If interest is paid in cash from the outset, the monthly Mezzanine Loan interest is $95,833, is not in the budget, and Borrower has no cash with which to pay it (Issue 5).

Every coverage figure in the record is a **senior-only** figure. On a combined basis, using the Appraiser's Stabilized NOI and the Credit Memorandum's 4.35% SOFR assumption: combined debt service is $3,728,750 senior + $1,509,375 mezzanine = **$5,238,125**, and combined coverage is **0.93x**. Combined debt at stabilization would be $47,500,000 + $12,075,000 = $59,575,000, or **78.18%** of the $76,200,000 as-stabilized value, and the combined debt yield is **8.19%** (senior-only debt yield 10.27%). The property does not cover total debt service from operations; the mini-perm exit depends on refinance proceeds, not on cash flow.

**Recommendation.** (a) Require disclosure of the Mezzanine Loan's full payment mechanics before closing, and require quarterly reporting of accreted balances (Draft § 16.4). (b) Add a **debt yield covenant** of not less than 8.50% (Draft § 8.4) — a rate-insensitive measure, which the Term Sheet lacks entirely. (c) Require a formal take-out/refinancing analysis at lease-up and as a condition to the Extension Option, including the combined leverage ratio. (d) Do not represent in the credit file that the Loan is self-liquidating; on a whole-loan basis it is not.

**Draft reference:** § 16.4 (with the computation noted), § 8.4, Exhibit G(k).

### Issue 7 — Loan Proceeds Fund a $1,835,000 Developer Fee Payable to the Borrower Before Any Equity Is at Risk

**Severity: High.**

**Sources:** Term Sheet § 5.2 (Developer Fee $2,835,000, "5% of total project cost"); § 14 (no distributions during the Construction Period "except for payment of the developer fee in accordance with the approved Project Budget"); Draw Schedule Detailed Budget line 5.01 (Vendor: **Harborview Capital Partners LLC**; Senior Loan $1,835,000; Mezzanine Loan $1,000,000); Draw Schedule "Draw Schedule" worksheet, draws 6 through 9 (Developer Fee allocated).

**Finding.** The Developer Fee is 5.00% of Total Project Costs and is payable to **Borrower itself**. $1,835,000 of it is funded by the senior Loan and $1,000,000 by the Mezzanine Loan. Combined with Issue 5, the economics are: the loans fund 100% of costs, of which 5% ($2,835,000) flows to the sponsor-controlled Borrower as a fee. That is not equity in any sense; it is negative equity.

The Term Sheet's distribution carve-out is also incoherent as drafted. Borrower is the payee, so a developer fee paid to Borrower is not a Distribution at all (there is no transfer to a member); and if the fee is then distributed to members during the Construction Period, that **is** a Distribution that the carve-out prohibits. The Draft resolves this by defining "Distributions" to capture both (§ 1.1), permitting the fee only to Borrower (§ 6.11), and conditioning it.

**Recommendation.** (a) Defer the Developer Fee: it should be earned only on Substantial Completion, and paid only if no Cost Overrun, no Interest Reserve deficiency, no unfunded equity obligation and no Event of Default exists, and only after the Construction Inspector confirms sufficient funds to complete. (b) Cap the senior-funded portion at the $1,835,000 allocated in the budget and prohibit payment of the $1,000,000 mezzanine-funded portion from Loan proceeds. (c) Require that the fee be paid to Borrower and not to any member or Affiliate (already the budget's vendor, but should be a covenant). (d) Consider subordinating the entire fee to repayment of the Loan — the strongest available answer to the equity problem, and one the Bank can reasonably require given that it is lending 100% of cost.

**Draft reference:** § 6.11; § 7.5(a) and (d); definition of "Distributions" in § 1.1.
